admission_exercises.name: Admissions Exercise for International Students (AEIS)
admission_exercises.description: Centralised admissions test for international students (non-SC, non-PR) seeking admission to Primary 2–5 and Secondary 1–3 in Singapore government schools. Tests English and Mathematics proficiency.
admission_exercises.eligibility: International students not currently studying in a Singapore government school. Must meet age requirements for the level applied for.
admission_exercises.test_period: September each year (for following January entry)
important_notes: Passing the test does NOT guarantee a school place — depends on vacancies
Students are allocated to schools by MOE based on vacancies and residential address
No school choice is given — MOE assigns based on available places
Primary 1 and Primary 6 admission not available through AEIS
Secondary 4 and 5 admission not available through AEIS
Test is conducted in English only
International students cannot apply for GEP (Gifted Education Programme)
Student Pass required from ICA before commencing studies

admission_exercises.name: Supplementary Admissions Exercise for International Students (S-AEIS)
admission_exercises.description: Supplementary round of AEIS for international students who missed the September AEIS or were unsuccessful. Tests for Primary 2–4 and Secondary 1–2 only (P5 and S3 not available in S-AEIS).
admission_exercises.eligibility: International students not placed through AEIS. Same criteria as AEIS.
admission_exercises.test_period: February–March each year (for same-year April entry)
important_notes: Fewer levels available than AEIS: only P2–P4 and S1–S2
P5 and S3 are NOT available in S-AEIS — must wait for next AEIS cycle
Same test format as AEIS
Placement depends on remaining school vacancies after January intake

admission_exercises.name: JC/MI Direct Admission for International Students
admission_exercises.description: International students seeking JC or Millennia Institute admission apply directly to schools in December, typically after completing IGCSE, O-Levels, or equivalent.
admission_exercises.eligibility: International students with equivalent qualifications (IGCSE, foreign O-Level equivalent, etc.)
important_notes: Must have equivalent of O-Level passes in relevant subjects
Schools assess individually — no centralised test
Student Pass required
Limited international student places at JCs

admission_exercises.name: Polytechnic Direct Admissions Exercise (DAE) for International Students
admission_exercises.description: International students with local or international qualifications can apply to polytechnics through DAE. Each polytechnic manages its own DAE.
admission_exercises.eligibility: International students with O-Levels, IGCSE, or equivalent qualifications
important_notes: Each polytechnic has its own DAE application portal
Course-specific requirements apply
International student quota applies — limited places
Full international student fees apply (no MOE subsidy unless under Tuition Grant scheme)

fee_structure.description: MOE differentiates school fees by citizenship/residency status. Fees increase in tiers: Singapore Citizen (lowest) → PR → International ASEAN → International non-ASEAN (highest).

fee_tiers.notes: Heavily subsidised. Misc fees only. No tuition fees at primary/secondary level.
Fees have been increasing annually as part of MOE's fee adjustment roadmap. Additional misc fees apply.
ASEAN member state nationals. Student Pass required from ICA.
Non-ASEAN international students pay the highest fees. Student Pass required from ICA.

fee_structure.independent_school_fees: Independent schools (e.g., RI, HCI, SCGS, NJC, ACSI) set their own fees — typically SGD 300–500/month for SC, SGD 750–1100 for PR, SGD 1700–2900 for international students.

university_fees.singapore_citizen: SGD 8,000–12,500 per year (subsidised, with Tuition Grant)
university_fees.international_with_tuition_grant: SGD 17,500–28,000 per year (must serve 3-year bond in Singapore-registered company after graduation)
university_fees.international_without_tuition_grant: SGD 30,000–60,000+ per year (unsubsidised; varies by course, especially Medicine/Dentistry)

tuition_grant_scheme.description: The MOE Tuition Grant (TG) subsidises university tuition for international students at Singapore's autonomous universities. In return, students must sign a bond to work in a Singapore-registered company for 3 years after graduation.
tuition_grant_scheme.eligibility: International students admitted to full-time undergraduate programmes at NUS, NTU, SMU, SUTD, SIT, SUSS.
tuition_grant_scheme.bond_duration: 3 years working in a Singapore-registered company
important_notes: Tuition Grant is NOT automatic — students must apply and be approved
Bond requires working at any Singapore-registered company (not limited to specific sectors)
Breaking the bond requires repaying the full grant amount with interest
TG does not cover Medicine and Dentistry for most international students
TG amount varies by course and university — check individual university websites

p1_registration.description: PR children participate in P1 Registration Exercise but at lower priority than Singapore Citizens.
phases_eligible: Phase 2C (if eligible, after all SC applicants)
important_notes: Phase 1–2B: Singapore Citizens only
Phase 2C: SCs balloted first if oversubscribed; remaining places then open to PRs
Phase 3: International students (on valid passes) apply if places remain
Home-school distance (within 1km / 1–2km) still matters for PR applicants
Singapore Citizens always have priority over PRs in balloting at every phase
PR children must register during the designated registration window

secondary_posting.description: PR students participate in S1 Posting Exercise after PSLE on the same merit basis as Singapore Citizens. However, in the event of a tie-breaker, Singapore Citizens are given priority.
important_notes: PR students sit the same PSLE exam as citizens
Same PSLE AL scoring and S1 posting process
Tie-breaker favours Singapore Citizens
Affiliation priority for PR students applies if their sibling is in the affiliated school

post_secondary.description: PR students participate in JAE (Joint Admissions Exercise) for JC, Polytechnic, and ITE admission on the same basis as citizens. Fee differences apply.
important_notes: Same JAE application process and merit-based posting
PR fees at JC/Poly/ITE are higher than citizen fees but still subsidised
Edusave benefits: PRs receive Edusave contributions but at lower rates than citizens
NS obligation: Male PRs may have NS obligation affecting university/work timelines

university.description: PR students apply to local autonomous universities on the same academic criteria as citizens. Fee differences apply. Eligible for MOE Tuition Grant without the 3-year bond (unlike international students).
important_notes: PR students pay higher tuition than SCs but lower than international students
PRs are eligible for MOE Tuition Grant without a work bond
PRs may apply for some (not all) bursaries and financial aid schemes
Some merit scholarships are open to PRs; many government scholarships are SC-only
Male PRs who have completed NS are treated same as SCs for admission timing

entry_points.description: Pass AEIS/S-AEIS test → placed in a government school → follow Singapore national curriculum → sit PSLE / N-levels / O-levels → JAE to JC/Poly/ITE
entry_points.suitable_for: International students aged 7–16 seeking mainstream Singapore education
entry_points.duration_to_university: Depends on entry point. E.g., entering at Sec 1 → 4 years to O-levels → 2 years JC → university = ~6–7 years

entry_points.pathway: International School → IB / IGCSE / AP → University
entry_points.description: Enrol in an international school → follow IB/IGCSE/AP curriculum → apply to Singapore or international universities
entry_points.suitable_for: Expat families, families wanting specific curricula, students who may return to home country
entry_points.duration_to_university: Typically 12–13 years total schooling (same as most countries)
cons: May not integrate into Singapore's national system
IB/AP scores need conversion for local university admission

entry_points.description: Apply directly to polytechnics with international qualifications (IGCSE, O-Level equivalent, etc.)
entry_points.suitable_for: International students aged 16+ with completed secondary education
entry_points.duration_to_university: 3 years polytechnic → DAE to university = ~6–7 years total post-secondary
pros: Pathway to local university via DAE
cons: Full international fees unless Tuition Grant
Limited international student quota at polys

entry_points.description: Apply to Singapore autonomous universities with IB, A-levels (from any country), AP, or other recognised international qualifications
entry_points.suitable_for: International students who have completed pre-university education abroad or at an international school
entry_points.duration_to_university: Direct entry (3–5 years depending on course)
cons: 3-year work bond if accepting Tuition Grant
Some courses (Medicine, Law) have very limited international student intake

ib_to_local_university_conversion.description: Singapore autonomous universities accept IB Diploma scores. Conversion to equivalent rank points varies by university and faculty.

general_guidelines.nus_ntu_competitive_courses: IB 40+ (out of 45) for Medicine, Law, Computing
general_guidelines.smu: IB 35+ for most courses; interview required
general_guidelines.sutd: IB 34+ plus design portfolio for some courses

important_notes: IB score requirements are approximate — check university admissions pages annually
Higher Level (HL) subjects given more weight than Standard Level (SL)
Subject prerequisites apply (e.g., HL Mathematics for Engineering/Computing)
Bonus points may apply for bilingualism or Theory of Knowledge (TOK)
Extended Essay and TOK grades can boost applications at some universities

student_pass.description: All international students (non-SC, non-PR) must hold a valid Student Pass (STP) issued by the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA) to study in Singapore.
student_pass.application_process: Apply via ICA's Student's Pass Online Application & Registration (SOLAR) system after receiving a school offer letter.
requirements: Valid offer letter from a registered educational institution
Valid passport with at least 6 months validity
Application fee (approximately SGD 30 processing + SGD 60 issuance)
important_notes: Student Pass must be renewed annually
Pass holders cannot work without a valid work pass (limited exceptions for university students)
University students on Student Pass may work part-time (up to 16 hours/week during term) at approved institutions
Breaking Student Pass conditions can result in cancellation and deportation
Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) holders do not need a Student Pass

fsbb_info.description: Full Subject-Based Banding (FSBB) replaces the Express, Normal Academic, and Normal Technical streams from the 2024 Secondary 1 cohort onwards.
key_changes: Students are placed in Posting Groups 1, 2, or 3 (replacing N(T), N(A), Express labels)
Subjects are taken at G1, G2, or G3 levels (G3 = most demanding, equivalent to old Express level)
Students can take different subjects at different G-levels based on ability
Mixed-form classes for non-academic subjects — students from all posting groups learn together
Common curriculum for certain subjects in lower secondary
New Secondary Education Certificate (SEC) exam will replace separate N-Level and O-Level exams

g_level_mapping.G1: Maps to old Normal Technical level
g_level_mapping.G2: Maps to old Normal Academic level

timeline.2024: First cohort placed in Posting Groups instead of streams
timeline.2027: First FSBB cohort sits national exams (new SEC exam expected)
timeline.2028: New Post-Secondary Admissions Exercise (PSE) expected to replace JAE for FSBB cohorts

impact_on_pathways: Students have more flexibility to take subjects at higher or lower levels
Reduces stigma of being in N(T) or N(A) stream
Pathway to JC/Poly/ITE will depend on G-level subjects taken and grades achieved
Details of new admissions criteria still being finalised by MOE
